hook: "Best creative formats on Meta for each funnel stage:"
body: William Kast maps creative formats to funnel stages: TOF gets founders ad, UGC, AI animation, yapper ad, native statics, long-form VSL, podcasts, 3 reasons why, and voiceless text overlay; MOF gets comment reply, testimonial mashup, raw honest review, review static, text wall; BOF gets urgency offer statics and product statics.
idea: Voiceless text overlay is a top-of-funnel format — match the format to the awareness stage.
sequencing: TOF: founders, UGC, AI animation, yapper, native statics, long VSL, podcasts, 3 reasons, voiceless text overlay.
MOF: comment reply, testimonial mashup, raw honest review, review static, text wall.
BOF: urgency offer statics, product statics.
The principle: format-stage fit beats format quality.
formatting: X list post organized by funnel stage.
why_it_works: Format-stage fit beats format quality — the right format at the wrong stage still fails.
what_to_steal: LC's funnel map: voiceless overlay for cold audiences, urgency statics for hot ones.

hook: "If you haven't tested these ad formats yet, you should:"
body: William Kast's 5 formats to test, with voiceless B-roll ads at #2: a mix of B-roll and product shots with no one talking, the script delivered through text overlay bullet points. Clean, fast, easy to scale.
idea: Voiceless B-roll is the scalable TOF workhorse — the script becomes text bullets over footage.
sequencing: Founder talking head: raw, 30s genuine talk beats polished.
Voiceless B-roll: B-roll plus product shots, no talking, script as text overlay bullets.
Yapper: uncut organic talking builds trust fastest.
AI educational: for health brands.
Camouflage: native image plus long emotional story.
The reframe: format gets attention, message gets conversion.
why_it_works: No talking means no creator bottleneck, no language barrier, and infinitely re-cuttable footage.
what_to_steal: LC's voiceless template: jewelry B-roll plus benefit bullets — no creator bottleneck.

hook: "one creative format is running 60%+ hook rate and CPMs 30% below account average for us right now."
body: Hannah Parvaz reports one creative format running a 60%+ hook rate with CPMs 30% below the account average: b-roll plus text overlay. 'Simple beats produced.'
idea: B-roll plus text overlay delivers 60%+ hook rates at 30% below-average CPMs — simple beats produced.
sequencing: The numbers: 60%+ hook rate, CPMs 30% below average.
The format: b-roll plus text overlay.
The principle: simple beats produced.
The implication: make it the cheapest-reach format in the account.
why_it_works: Simplicity reads as content, not advertising — the algorithm rewards it with cheap reach.
what_to_steal: Make b-roll + text overlay LC's cheapest-reach format and measure it on hook rate and CPM.

hook: "This reel format got 800k views and 1M views for Gamma, a $1B AI powerpoint company"
body: Annie Yang breaks down a reel format that got 800k and 1M views for Gamma, a $1B AI powerpoint company: a simple 7-8 second UGC clip with text overlay, spinning a funny story with a Gamma mention (plus another mention in the comments). Great for brand awareness — and no comments accusing the video of being an ad.
idea: A funny 7-second story with a soft brand mention plus a comment mention is a million-view awareness unit.
sequencing: The results: 800k and 1M views for Gamma.
The format: 7-8 second UGC clip with text overlay.
The story: funny, with a soft Gamma mention.
The second mention: in the comments.
The job: brand awareness.
The proof of nativeness: no comments accusing it of being an ad.
formatting: X text post with a reel link.
why_it_works: The joke earns the view; the brand mention rides along unnoticed — and comments stay clean because it never feels like an ad.
what_to_steal: LC's 7-second funny-story reels with a soft LC mention plus a comment mention.

body: YourAvgTechBro's two working formats: (1) hook and demo video — AI avatar plus spicy text hook, then the product demo; (2) text on screen — hook+demo without the demo: a background clip with a long text block, less conversion-oriented, more useful for brand awareness and account health.
idea: Text-on-screen is the awareness companion to hook+demo's conversion — run both lanes.
sequencing: Format 1: hook and demo — AI avatar + spicy text hook, then product demo.
Format 2: text on screen — background clip + long text block, no demo.
The split: conversion vs brand awareness and account health.
The voiceless lesson: text-on-screen buys cheap reach while hook+demo buys sales.
why_it_works: Text-on-screen buys cheap reach and account health while hook+demo buys sales — different jobs, different formats.
what_to_steal: LC's two-lane system: hook+demo for conversion, text-on-screen for cheap reach.

sequencing: Headline promise: 30 scroll-stopping formats.

Creative and Bonus folders complete the tree.

hook: "Most important components of a winning ad in order:"
body: Jakob Counts ranks the most important components of a winning ad, in order: clarity, messaging, text overlay hook, visual hook, visual format, relatability, proof/trust, urgency. Asks what others would add.
idea: The text overlay hook is the #3 component of a winning ad — ranked above the visual hook itself.
sequencing: #1 Clarity.
#2 Messaging.
#3 Text overlay hook.
#4 Visual hook.
#5 Visual format.
#6 Relatability.
#7 Proof/trust; #8 Urgency.
The engagement question: what would you add.
formatting: Ranked X list post with an engagement question.
why_it_works: Text overlay does the clarifying work the visual can't — it names the promise the footage only implies.
what_to_steal: Use this exact order as LC's creative QA checklist — clarity and messaging before any visual work.

hook: "‼️Tiktok Outlier Alert ‼️ 📉 585K Views, 133K Likes, 322 Comments, 28K Shares, 11K Saves"

The hook contrasts a positive relationship state with an immediate obstacle; the shift from beautiful real-life dining footage to a simple phone widget is a native product placement that feels like a shared coping mechanism, not an ad.
cta: implicit — "copy it and do the same"
idea: Silent emotional b-roll plus a text hook plus native demo placement is the voiceless ad perfected.
sequencing: The stats block.
The b-roll: silent, intimate travel and dinner footage.
The text hook: long-distance relationship tension.
The demo: the shared couples drawing widget.
Why it works: the obstacle-plus-coping-mechanism framing.
The nudge: copy the structure.
formatting: X outlier-alert post with an emoji stats block.
why_it_works: Silence plus beauty plus a relatable obstacle lets the viewer project their own story onto the footage — the product placement feels like a coping mechanism, not an ad.
what_to_steal: LC's silent aesthetic b-roll — jewelry in water, on skin — plus a text hook, with the product as the answer.

hook: "the 5 ad creative formats that convert highest in dropshipping right now ranked by performance:"
body: Alex Page's ranked list of the 5 highest-converting dropship formats, with #5 being slideshow with text overlays: 5-7 product images with benefit text on each, 'problem → solution → proof → offer,' works on Meta Stories and Reels, lowest production cost of all formats — 15 minutes to make, converting at 70-80% of video performance for 5% of the effort.
idea: A 15-minute text-overlay slideshow converts at 70–80% of video for 5% of the effort — the highest-ROI creative.
sequencing: #1 UGC problem/solution.
#2 'TikTok made me buy it.'
#3 us-vs-them split screen.
#4 founder talking head — the face IS the retargeting.
#5 slideshow with text overlays: 5-7 images, benefit text, problem→solution→proof→offer.
The common thread: native feel; the best ad doesn't look like an ad.
why_it_works: The effort-to-performance ratio is the whole pitch — slideshows are cheap, fast, and nearly as good as video.
what_to_steal: LC's 15-minute slideshow template: problem → solution → proof → offer, 5-7 jewelry images with benefit text.

idea: Long text-on-screen alone is the worst-converting format — it needs b-roll to work.
sequencing: #1 talking head.
#2 hook and demo.
#3 skit.
The massive wall.
#100 long text on screen.

why_it_works: Text without motion is a chore to read — the b-roll is what makes text overlay work at all.
what_to_steal: LC rule: never text-only — always text over moving b-roll.

body: William Kast's creative-diversity SOP: (1) take your winning message; (2) rewrite it as a podcast ad, street-interview ad, native talking no-cuts ad, traditional UGC ad, mute text overlay ad, and a ton of static ads; (3) pair each script with 3 different hooks; (4) launch and watch the account scale. Each creative style reaches a different pocket of the audience.
idea: The mute text overlay is one of six skins for the same winning message — each with 3 hooks.
sequencing: Step 1: take your winning message.
Step 2: rewrite it as podcast, street interview, native no-cuts, UGC, mute text overlay, and statics.
Step 3: pair each script with 3 different hooks.
Step 4: launch and watch the account scale.
The principle: each style reaches a different pocket of the audience.
why_it_works: Same message, different skins — creative diversity without new thinking.
what_to_steal: LC's repackaging SOP: every winner gets a mute-text-overlay version × 3 hooks.

hook: "The fastest way to waste money on Meta is running the right ad at the wrong awareness level."
body: Dennis maps formats to awareness levels: unaware gets founder ad, podcast clip, yapper ad, AI animation, voiceless text overlay (pitching product to the unaware is the failure mode); problem-aware gets UGC, native statics, 3 reasons why; solution-aware gets long-form VSL, text wall; product-aware gets raw honest review, testimonial mashup, comment reply, review static; most-aware gets urgency offer static, product static. Same product, five different ads.
idea: Voiceless text overlay is an unaware-stage format — don't pitch product to people who haven't admitted the problem.
sequencing: Unaware: founder, podcast, yapper, AI animation, voiceless text overlay.
Problem-aware: UGC, native statics, 3 reasons why.
Solution-aware: long-form VSL, text wall.
Product-aware: raw honest review, testimonial mashup, comment reply, review static.
Most-aware: urgency offer static, product static.
The rule: same product, five different ads.
formatting: X map post with failure modes per stage.
why_it_works: Awareness mismatch is the silent budget killer — the map names the failure mode per stage.
what_to_steal: LC's awareness map: voiceless overlay only for cold audiences; never pitch product to the unaware.

hook: "Meta can treat your 20 ads as one ad."
body: Oussama's creative-diversity warning: Meta can treat your 20 ads as one ad. Same footage, same hook, different text overlay is variation, not testing. Real creative diversity means a different first 3 seconds, a different angle, a different pace, a different person on screen. The Q4 check: 'Would a stranger think these are different ads?' If not, you didn't test anything.
idea: Text-overlay swaps on identical footage don't count as creative testing — Andromeda deduplicates them.
sequencing: The claim: Meta treats 20 lookalike ads as one ad.
What isn't testing: same footage, same hook, different text overlay.
What real diversity looks like: different first 3 seconds, angle, pace, person.
The stranger test: would a stranger think these are different ads.
The Q4 warning: if not, you didn't test anything.
why_it_works: Andromeda deduplicates lookalike creative — fake variety wastes the test budget.
what_to_steal: LC's pre-batch stranger test: would a stranger think these are different ads?

body: Carly North's observation: UGC is changing — it used to be about looking effortless and unpolished, but the content winning now is way more intentional: better cuts, more visuals, text overlays. Produced doesn't have to mean polished; it just has to keep attention without feeling like an ad.
idea: The new UGC is intentional — text overlays and sharp cuts are the production value now.
sequencing: The shift: UGC used to be effortless and unpolished.
What's winning now: intentional — better cuts, more visuals, text overlays.
The reframe: produced doesn't mean polished.
The bar: keep attention without feeling like an ad.
why_it_works: Audiences got literate — effortless now reads as lazy; intentional-but-native wins.
what_to_steal: LC's UGC brief: intentional cuts plus text overlays, still native-feeling.
